articles.title: Your cache key is a specification
articles.thesis: A cache key enumerates everything the render depends on, so getting it wrong is a correctness bug rather than a performance one.
articles.evidence_summary: The locale and error-page incidents are both cases of an input missing from the key; the determinism argument explains why the key can be trusted at all.
articles.reader_knowledge_assumed: Familiarity with HTTP caching and cache invalidation as a concept; no knowledge of this pipeline.
articles.platform_fit: Fits a 1500-2000 word personal-blog post with two concrete failure stories.

articles.title: Determinism is what makes caching a latency win
articles.thesis: Caching only converts to latency instead of staleness when the computation being cached is deterministic for its inputs.
articles.evidence_summary: The 78% profiling number motivates the cache; the determinism observation is what made it viable.
articles.reader_knowledge_assumed: Comfortable with profiling output and the idea of a pure function.
articles.platform_fit: Shorter, more conceptual; risks being thin without the incident material from the first article.

competing_theses: The story could be told as an incident writeup rather than as a design argument, but the source has no timeline detail and the postmortem is unpublishable.

series.sequencing_rationale: The concrete failure lands first; the conceptual piece reads as the generalisation of it rather than as preamble.

decision.rationale: The cache-key argument carries the strongest evidence and the material the source actually documents; the determinism piece depends on it for concreteness.

alternatives_considered.description: One long article covering both the incident and the determinism argument.
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: At practitioner depth it would exceed the 1800-word target and bury the incident detail that makes the argument land.

alternatives_considered.description: An incident writeup structured as a timeline.
alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: The source has no minute-by-minute detail, and the internal postmortem is marked unpublishable.

uncertainties: Whether the determinism article has enough independent material to stand alone, or should be a section of the first.
